To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the usage of the TCR V region repertoire in psoriasis does not show any differences between type I and type II.
the usage of the TCR variable regions in psoriasis is similar in both type I and type II, and that the usage of these variable regions does not differ from that of healthy controls.
The TCR repertoire is not altered in psoriasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a T cell mediated immunological reaction, but it cannot be concluded that the TCR repertoire is involved in the pathogenesis of psoriasis.
the question as to whether the TCR repertoire in psoriatic skin shows a positive or negative selection of particular V regions.
the question of whether TCR V regions can be used as markers for the selection of a specific T cell population in psoriasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the usage of TCR V regions in psoriasis is similar to that in normal skin.
the TCR V region usage in psoriasis is similar in both forms and that the T cells in psoriasis do not seem to be selected by a positive or negative selection process.
the usage of V beta 5.2 and V beta 12 was significantly higher in psoriasis compared to healthy controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TCR V regions under investigation are not differentially used in type I and type II.
the TCR repertoire in psoriasis is not restricted and that the V regions are not differentially expressed in the two forms.
the TCR repertoire is not altered in the psoriatic skin and therefore the T cells in psoriasis do not show a clonal expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TCR repertoire of psoriatic T cells is not restricted.
the pathogenetic role of T cells cannot be explained by a selection of the TCR V regions under investigation.
T cells in type I and type II show a similar repertoire of TCR V regions and therefore a comparable pathogenetic potential.
